title: Store-side recovery binding schema and atomic recovery-install transaction surface
description:
Objective: give @moe/store the rows and the public atomic transaction surface that a recovery install needs, and resolve the dependency-direction question that currently makes task-b6e3dd2a unsatisfiable. Authored by governor-36019faa on human direction 2026-08-10 from two independent architect audits on task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683.

THE BLOCKER THIS EXISTS TO REMOVE, measured at HEAD bec1cc6 by governor-36019faa:
1. packages/store/package.json has NO "dependencies" field AT ALL. Full file is name, version, private, type, exports, scripts. @moe/store therefore cannot import @moe/core - which owns reduceProject(recovery.restore_quiesce) - and must not import upward from apps/daemon.
2. grep -rln "incarnation|key_epoch|keyEpoch" packages/store/src/ returns NOTHING.
3. The store schema holds exactly: aggregate_heads, command_receipts, domain_events, outbox_messages, store_metadata, command_decisions, store_project_binding, command_receipt_scopes, projections, inbox_receipts, event_subscriptions, cursor_generations. No recovery-incarnation, key-epoch, credential, grant, or project-lifecycle rows. Exact schema validation REJECTS extra tables/metadata, so rows cannot be added ad hoc by a consumer.

THE ARCHITECTURE QUESTION THE ARCHITECT MUST SETTLE FIRST, and it is genuinely open - do not assume the answer. Either (a) @moe/store legitimately declares a dependency on @moe/core, or (b) the binding codec lives in a lower shared package both can depend on, or (c) the anchor does not belong in @moe/store at all. Option (a) is a real layering change and must be justified, not slipped in as a manifest line. Record the decision and its reasoning in planningNotes; a later reader must be able to see why the edge is legitimate rather than expedient.

RELATED PRIOR ART to read before naming files: apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts already exists. Establish whether it is the codec this task should move/share or an unrelated surface, and say which. Landing a second binding codec is the silent-duplicate failure the staleness rail warns about.

NOT IN SCOPE: the two-slot installer protocol itself (task-b6e3dd2a), the durable key provider, the daemon restore controller, generating backup bytes.

Hard dependencies: the durable OS-protected recovery key provider task (order 13.01, same epic) must be DONE, because the key-epoch column has no meaning until an epoch survives restart. This task is BACKLOG until then. If claim_next_task serves it before that task is DONE, block it immediately and cite this line rather than re-deriving.

Owned paths: packages/store/src/ (schema migration, binding codec, recovery-install transaction surface, export wiring) plus packages/store/package.json if the architect's decision is option (a).

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test
definitionOfDone: The dependency-direction decision is recorded with its justification, and the resulting edge is proven three ways: the consuming manifest declares it, pnpm-lock.yaml carries the importer entry, and a compiled bare-specifier probe typechecks and is deleted in the same command.

A schema migration adds the recovery binding rows the installer requires; exact schema validation accepts the new shape and still rejects unknown tables and metadata, with a test pinning both directions.

A public atomic recovery-install transaction surface exists on @moe/store: one transaction commits the binding, and a partial or interrupted install leaves the prior state intact rather than a mixed state.
Every refusal asserts its exact stable reason code AND the refusing layer; each declared failure injection is generated at least once and the suite fails if a sweep produces zero cases.
A migration applied to an existing populated database preserves prior rows, proven by a test that writes before migrating and reads back after.
Mutating each production guard turns a NAMED focused test red; drills run, reverted, exact failing assertions recorded.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test exits 0.
taskRails: Authoritative design is D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-rebuild-design.md SHA-256 1D9D1EC97D3F07247FBBC088045E0BA2FD6DA8307F10A9026C55106419383191; do not edit it.
@moe/store must NOT import upward from apps/daemon under any circumstance. If the needed surface only exists there, that is a blocker to report, not a shortcut to take.
Do not reimplement lifecycle or business authority inside the store. The store holds rows and transactions; reduceProject remains @moe/core's.

Cross-package symbol use must prove the DEPENDENCY EDGE, not just the symbol: manifest, lockfile importer, compiled bare-specifier probe. This task exists partly because that check was skipped elsewhere.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; this cap is per file, never per task.

MIGRATION + TRANSACTION MACHINERY READ (all four named files plus the ones the plan did not name):
- sqlite-schema-manifest.ts: SCHEMA_V1_OBJECT_SQL -> SCHEMA_V2_OBJECT_SQL (spread) -> SCHEMA_OBJECT_SQL (spread). Additive-by-spread is the established idiom.
- sqlite-schema-migration.ts (157 lines): migrateLocked -> installFreshSchema | migrateV1ToV2 | migrateV2ToV3. BOTH existing migrations REFUSE populated databases with STORE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED via hasDurableRows(). My v3->v4 leg must NOT copy that: DoD 5 requires a populated database to migrate and preserve rows, which is achievable because adding tables touches no existing row.
- sqlite-schema-conformance.ts (73 lines): validateExactSchemaObjects counts sqlite_schema rows and compares normalized SQL per object -> extra table = STORE_SCHEMA_INVALID. validateSchemaManifestMetadata requires store_metadata to hold EXACTLY ONE row (schema_manifest_version). So the migration must NOT add a metadata row, and cannot smuggle tables past the check.
- sqlite-schema-bootstrap.ts (227 lines): bootstrapAndValidateSchema wraps isFreshDatabase + migrateLocked + validateSchema + resolveProjectBinding in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, with OUTCOME_UNKNOWN on an unprovable commit.
- sqlite-schema-integrity.ts (215 lines): validateSchema, called on every open.
- store-runtime.ts (301 lines): StoreRuntime base holds `protected database`, requireOpen/readOperation/normalizeOperationalError/poison. This is the seam the atomic surface will compose.
- decision-ledger-transaction.ts (201 lines): the canonical BEGIN IMMEDIATE / commitAttempted / classifyDecisionFailure -> OUTCOME_UNKNOWN + poison() discipline. Reuse this shape, do not hand-roll a second one.
- decision-ledger.ts (130 lines): DecisionLedgerStore extends DecisionTransactionStore; createDecisionLedgerCore exposes a frozen DecisionLedgerCore facade that SqliteEventStore delegates to. SqliteEventStore is Object.freeze'd and holds the core in a private #core, so an external module CANNOT reach the DatabaseSync. The atomic surface therefore has to enter the ledger class chain, not sit beside it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR STEP 4 (measured, decides the migration shape): exact validation + the one-row metadata rule mean new tables REQUIRE a SCHEMA_VERSION bump 3 -> 4 and SQLITE_SCHEMA_MANIFEST_VERSION "moe-sqlite-schema/3" -> "/4". Existing tests that pin the old numbers and will need updating: store-schema-v3-migration.test.ts (user_version 3 x3, "moe-sqlite-schema/3" x2, toHaveLength(14), validateExactSchemaObjects(...,3), and the "refuses a newer schema version" tamper that writes user_version = 4), command-decision-integrity.test.ts:184 (user_version: 3), store-project-and-schema-contract.test.ts:65,86 (PRAGMA user_version = 4 as the "too new" value). implementationPlan.description:
SETTLE THE ARCHITECTURE QUESTION — DoD 1, and the task says it is genuinely open. My measured recommendation is NONE OF (a)/(b)/(c) AS FRAMED: **no dependency edge is required at all.** Verify this before accepting it, and record the decision with its reasoning in your completion notes either way.

THE REASONING. The premise behind the question is that @moe/store needs @moe/core because core owns reduceProject(recovery.restore_quiesce). It does not. taskRail 3 states the split precisely: "The store holds rows and transactions; reduceProject remains @moe/core's." This task lands exactly three things — recovery binding ROWS, a byte-level CODEC, and an atomic TRANSACTION surface. None performs lifecycle reasoning, so none needs the reducer. The composition of reducer + store is the DAEMON's job and belongs to task-2ff368fe (13.03), which already depends on both.

Option (a) store -> core would invert the layering: a storage package would gain a dependency on business logic and inherit everything core pulls in. Option (c) is wrong because the rows genuinely belong in the store — durable rows plus an atomic transaction is precisely what a store is for.

MEASURED LAYERING that makes the fallback safe if you find I am wrong: @moe/contracts has NO dependencies (it is the root layer), @moe/core depends on @moe/contracts, @moe/store depends on nothing. So IF the store turns out to genuinely need a shared symbol, declare @moe/contracts — acyclic and matching how core already layers — and NEVER @moe/core.

CONSEQUENCE FOR DoD 1's three-way edge proof: if the decision is "no edge", that clause has no subject. Prove the NEGATIVE instead and say so — packages/store/package.json still declares no dependencies and the package typechecks and tests clean without one. If you do add @moe/contracts, then the full three-way proof applies: manifest declaration, pnpm-lock.yaml importer entry, and a compiled bare-specifier probe deleted in the same command.

PRIOR ART, and this is a duplicate-codec hazard the task names explicitly. apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts has `encodeBinding` (:40) and `decodeBinding` (:88) — both MODULE-PRIVATE, only readAnchoredIncarnation (:147) and anchorIncarnation (:186) are exported — inside a module that imports `{ CommandDecisionRecord, SqliteEventStore } from "@moe/store"`. It is a daemon-side CONSUMER of the store, so the store cannot reuse it without importing upward, which taskRail 2 forbids absolutely. Your codec is therefore a second implementation BY NECESSITY. Do not pretend otherwise: state it in completion notes as a DECLARED duplicate with a retirement path, and name the follow-on that should migrate the daemon onto the store's canonical codec. A silent second codec is the failure the staleness rail warns about; a declared one with an owner is not.
implementationPlan.note:
DECISION (DoD 1): **NO DEPENDENCY EDGE.** None of options (a)/(b)/(c) as framed. packages/store/package.json stays without a "dependencies" field.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED:
- `packages/contracts/package.json` -> dependencies undefined, devDependencies undefined. Root layer.
- `packages/core/package.json` -> dependencies {"@moe/contracts":"workspace:*"}.
- `packages/store/package.json` -> keys exactly [name, version, private, type, exports, scripts]; dependencies undefined.
- `grep -rn 'from "@moe/' packages/store/src` exits 1 — ZERO cross-package imports today.
- `grep -rln restore_quiesce` -> packages/core/src/project/{project-contract,project-reducer,project-validation}.ts (+2 tests, +testkit table). reduceProject is core's, and it stays there.

JUSTIFICATION. The question's premise is that the store needs @moe/core because core owns reduceProject(recovery.restore_quiesce). It does not. This task lands three things and none of them reasons about lifecycle: (i) recovery binding ROWS, (ii) a byte-level CODEC over opaque payload bytes, (iii) an atomic TRANSACTION. The row shape I am landing is the STORE's own — slot, incarnation ref, key-epoch ref, digest, codec version, opaque payload BLOB, installed_at — so the daemon maps its RecoveryIncarnationBinding onto columns rather than the store importing the domain type. Composing reducer with store is the daemon's job (task-2ff368fe, 13.03), which already depends on both.

Option (a) rejected: a storage package depending on business logic inverts the layering and drags core's whole transitive graph in. Option (b) held but NOT exercised: store -> contracts would be acyclic (contracts is the root layer) but nothing in this task needs a shared symbol, so declaring it would be an unused edge. Option (c) rejected: durable rows plus an atomic transaction is exactly what a store is for.

PROOF OF THE NEGATIVE (DoD 1's three-way clause has no subject, so I prove the absence instead). At completion I will re-assert: packages/store/package.json still declares no "dependencies" key, packages/store/src still contains zero `from "@moe/..."` imports, and the package typechecks and tests clean. Baseline before any bytes: typecheck exit 0, test exit 0, 32 files / 357 tests.

DECLARED DUPLICATE CODEC (not silent). apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts:40 `function encodeBinding` and :88 `function decodeBinding` carry NO export keyword — only :147 readAnchoredIncarnation and :186 anchorIncarnation are exported — and that module's first line is `import type { CommandDecisionRecord, SqliteEventStore } from "@moe/store"`. It is a downstream CONSUMER of the store, so reuse would require @moe/store to import upward from apps/daemon, which taskRail 2 forbids absolutely. The store's codec is therefore a second implementation BY NECESSITY, and it is deliberately NOT the same codec: the daemon's encodes the full RecoveryIncarnationBinding JSON with an 11-key exact-shape decode; mine encodes a store row record whose payload is opaque bytes the store never interprets. They overlap only in that both frame a binding.

RETIREMENT PATH, to be created by an architect (I am not authorised to create board tasks): "Retire the daemon-private recovery binding codec onto @moe/store's canonical recovery-install surface" — scope apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts, delete its private encodeBinding/decodeBinding, and route anchoring through the store's installRecoveryBinding/readRecoveryBinding. It must not land before task-b6e3dd2a (the two-slot installer) settles the protocol, because that task decides what the daemon actually writes. I will post this to chat and as a task comment so it is not lost.

CLAUSE 1 CONSUMERS (named now, per taskRail): task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683 (two-slot anchor installer — consumes the atomic install surface and the codec) and task-2ff368fe2de44028b4a7d6ca89687933 (13.03 daemon restore controller — composes the same surface).

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED. Create the focused test for the schema migration and the binding rows. DoD 2 requires exact schema validation to ACCEPT the new shape and STILL REJECT unknown tables and metadata — pin BOTH directions, because a migration that loosens the conformance check to make room is the silent regression here. Assert the twelve existing tables are still present and still exactly validated.

DoD 5 is the clause most likely to be skipped: a migration applied to an EXISTING POPULATED database must preserve prior rows. Write rows through the production surface FIRST, then migrate, then read back and assert the earlier rows are byte-identical. A migration tested only against an empty database proves nothing about the upgrade path real deployments take.

Every refusal pins its exact stable reason code AND the refusing layer (DoD 4), and the generated sweep asserts a NON-ZERO case count.

Use a real temp path via mkdtemp under the OS temp root, never inside the repo, cleaned in an afterEach that runs on failure — this host is win32 and a stray .sqlite file in a commit breaks the no-scratch-files rail.
implementationPlan.note:
RED CONFIRMED: `pnpm --filter @moe/store test` exit 1 — "Test Files 4 failed | 32 passed (36), Tests 4 failed | 359 passed (363)". The four failures are exactly the four new files; the 32 pre-existing files still pass, so nothing was broken to make room.

1. recovery-install-codec.test.ts (DoD 4). BOTH sweep disciplines present. ENCODE_REFUSAL_CASES is HAND-WRITTEN (13 entries) and guarded by a separate hand-written ENCODE_REFUSAL_NAMES list plus a length equality, so deleting a case fails instead of shrinking the suite. The GENERATED sweeps each assert a NON-ZERO count AND pin it to the generator's own arity: every prefix truncation (count === bytes.length), every header-byte corruption (count === headerLength), every one-position digest deviation (count === 64). Every refusal asserts code AND layer, never merely "not ok".

2. GUARD ORDER PINNED EXPLICITLY — the rail's real subject. "answers a stale digest before it parses, and says so" feeds truncated bytes with the ORIGINAL digest and requires RECOVERY_BINDING_DIGEST_MISMATCH, not BYTES_MALFORMED, fixing decode order as digest-then-structure. Every generated structural sweep therefore RECOMPUTES the digest for its mutated bytes so the structural guard is genuinely reached. Without that recomputation the entire truncation sweep would have passed while testing only the digest gate.

3. recovery-install.test.ts (DoD 3). THE ATOMICITY TEST USES NO INJECTED SEAM. ACTIVE holds REF_X, PENDING holds REF_Y; installing REF_Y into ACTIVE trips the store's own UNIQUE(incarnation_ref) AFTER the slot row is deleted. Measured on node v24.16.0 node:sqlite first: errcode 2067, message "UNIQUE constraint failed", database.isTransaction still true after the failed statement, explicit ROLLBACK restores both prior rows. The assertion is not "it returned an error" but that ACTIVE still reads back REF_X with the SAME bindingDigest and SAME payload bytes after close and REOPEN. I deliberately deleted a test-only tamper method I had first written onto the frozen public class; the tamper test now UPDATEs binding_bytes through a second raw DatabaseSync, so no escape hatch is added to production. TWO-LAYER ORDER PINNED BOTH WAYS: on an UNSCOPED handle a MALFORMED record still refuses RECOVERY_INSTALL_SCOPE_REQUIRED at the transaction layer; on a SCOPED handle the same record refuses at the codec layer with its exact code. Store FAULTS stay faults: a closed handle throws DurableStoreError STORE_CLOSED.

4. store-schema-v4-migration.test.ts (DoD 2 and DoD 5). Both conformance directions pinned: v4 accepted, AND an extra table (recovery_grants) and an extra store_metadata row each still refuse STORE_SCHEMA_INVALID, asserted three ways — validateSchema, the specific conformance function, and a real store open. V3_TABLES is a hand-written 12-name list asserted present in both the frozen v3 manifest and the v4 manifest. DoD 5 fixture: rows written through the PRODUCTION surface (store.commit), then the file rewound to v3, and the fixture PROVEN VALID AT THE EARLIER LAYER before use — validateExactSchemaObjects(db, SCHEMA_V3_OBJECT_SQL, 3), validateSchemaManifestMetadata(db, "moe-sqlite-schema/3"), domain_events count 1. After migrating, raw domain_events and command_receipts row arrays are compared against the pre-migration snapshot.

5. recovery-install-entrypoint.test.ts + recovery-install-entrypoint-worker.mjs — the type-only-publication trap. The worker imports ./index.ts under --experimental-strip-types (the package's own probe pattern; "." in the exports map IS ./src/index.ts) and reports only RUNTIME values: typeof on encode/decode, typeof on SqliteEventStore.prototype.installRecoveryBinding and .readRecoveryBinding, the literal codec version, spread slot/layer arrays, the reason-code count, and a real encode-then-decode round trip. An `export type` publication makes every one of those undefined.

Temp paths: mkdtempSync under tmpdir() in every file, cleaned in an afterEach that runs on failure. No .sqlite artefact can reach the repo.

implementationPlan.description:
Land the schema migration: extend packages/store/src/sqlite-schema-manifest.ts with the recovery binding rows the installer requires, and wire the upgrade through the existing sqlite-schema-migration.ts rather than inventing a second path. Keep sqlite-schema-conformance.ts's exactness intact — the new tables become part of the expected set, and anything outside it must still be rejected.

Define the ROW SHAPE as the store's own, not a copy of the daemon's domain binding: the store persists columns and bytes, and the daemon maps its RecoveryIncarnationBinding onto them. That separation is what keeps the store free of an upward dependency and is the concrete form of the architecture decision from step 2.

Both files sit near the cap — sqlite-schema-manifest.ts is 234 physical lines against a 250 target — so if the new tables push it over, split the recovery rows into their own manifest module rather than overflowing. Measure with `grep -c ''`, never PowerShell Measure-Object -Line.
implementationPlan.note:
SCHEMA v4 LANDED. store-schema-v4-migration.test.ts now passes 4 of 5 — including the DoD 5 populated-database preservation test. The single remaining failure there is `migrated.installRecoveryBinding is not a function`, i.e. step 5's surface, not the migration.

ROW SHAPE — the store's OWN, per the step-2 decision. New file sqlite-schema-recovery-manifest.ts (36 lines) holds one table:
recovery_bindings(slot TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK slot IN ('ACTIVE','PENDING'), incarnation_ref TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE hex64-checked, key_epoch_ref TEXT NOT NULL hex64-checked, binding_codec_version TEXT NOT NULL, binding_digest TEXT NOT NULL hex64-checked, binding_bytes BLOB NOT NULL 1..MAX_BLOB_BYTES, installed_at TEXT NOT NULL) STRICT.
Columns the store can police itself are columns; everything the store must NOT interpret rides in one opaque blob. That is the concrete form of "no upward dependency": the daemon maps RecoveryIncarnationBinding onto these columns and keeps its lifecycle reasoning. `slot` is a bounded enum so a third slot cannot appear by accident. The two-slot installer PROTOCOL is not defined here — only the rows it needs plus the guarantee, via UNIQUE(incarnation_ref), that one incarnation cannot occupy both slots. That constraint is also what makes the DoD 3 atomicity test a real interruption instead of an injected one.

SPLIT RATHER THAN OVERFLOW, exactly as the step anticipated. sqlite-schema-manifest.ts was 234/250, so the table lives in its own module and the manifest only imports and spreads it. Measured with `grep -c ''`: sqlite-schema-manifest.ts 241, sqlite-schema-recovery-manifest.ts 36, sqlite-schema-migration.ts 176, store-internals.ts 131. All at or under the 250 target.

MANIFEST CHAIN. Today's SCHEMA_OBJECT_SQL was renamed SCHEMA_V3_OBJECT_SQL (frozen, 14 objects) and SCHEMA_OBJECT_SQL is now `{...SCHEMA_V3_OBJECT_SQL, ...SCHEMA_V4_RECOVERY_OBJECT_SQL}` (15 objects). No v3 object is redefined, which is what makes the new leg additive.

MIGRATION COMPOSED, NOT INVENTED. migrateV3ToV4 reuses the existing validateMigrationSource (whose schemaVersion parameter widened 1|2 -> 1|2|3), then one CREATE TABLE, then the existing metadata UPDATE and PRAGMA user_version pattern. migrateLocked became `if (v===1) v1->v2; if (v<=2) v2->v3; v3->v4`, so every historical source still reaches head.

IT IS THE ONLY LEG THAT ACCEPTS A POPULATED SOURCE, and deliberately so. v1->v2 and v2->v3 call hasDurableRows() and refuse with STORE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED because they rebuild domain_events and cannot reconcile rows they rewrite. v3->v4 creates one table and touches nothing existing, so it has nothing to reconcile — that is why DoD 5 is satisfiable here and was not there.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED WHILE WIRING: migrateV2ToV3 stamped SQLITE_SCHEMA_MANIFEST_VERSION and SCHEMA_VERSION, both of which now mean v4. Left alone, a v1 or v2 database would have been labelled v4 while carrying a v3 schema, and validateMigrationSource in the next leg would then have refused it. It now stamps the new SCHEMA_V3_MANIFEST_VERSION and a literal user_version 3, and its five CREATE statements reference SCHEMA_V3_OBJECT_SQL explicitly rather than riding on head. The empty-v1 and bound-empty-v2 legs in store-schema-v3-migration.test.ts pass, which is what proves the chain.

CONFORMANCE EXACTNESS UNTOUCHED. sqlite-schema-conformance.ts was not modified at all — no loosening was needed, because the new table joins the expected manifest instead of being excused from it. The v4 test asserts an extra table (recovery_grants) and an extra store_metadata row each still refuse STORE_SCHEMA_INVALID, three ways each.

VERSION-PIN UPDATES in four existing test files, applied by a scripted patch that ABORTS unless each literal appears the exact expected number of times, so nothing was silently missed or over-replaced: store-schema-v3-migration.test.ts (user_version 3->4 x3, manifest /3->/4 x2, SCHEMA_OBJECT_SQL length 14->15, validateExactSchemaObjects version arg 3->4 x2, "too new" tamper 4->5), command-decision-integrity.test.ts (getHealth().userVersion 3->4, user_version 3->4), store-project-and-schema-contract.test.ts ("too new" tamper 4->5 and its read-back), sqlite-event-store-core.test.ts (health.userVersion 3->4). The "refuses a newer schema version" guards were re-pointed at 5 rather than deleted, so that leg stays covered.

DISCLOSED, PRE-EXISTING, NOT MINE TO FIX HERE: store-contracts.ts is 297 lines, already over the 250 target before this task. My change to it is a single string literal ("moe-sqlite-schema/3" -> "/4") with zero net lines, so I did not restructure a file this task does not otherwise touch.

implementationPlan.description:
Land the binding codec plus the public atomic recovery-install transaction surface: packages/store/src/recovery-install.ts and its one-line LF `.js` bridge (every module in this package has one — check a sibling and match it byte-for-byte in form).

DoD 3 is the load-bearing property: ONE transaction commits the binding, and a partial or interrupted install leaves the PRIOR state intact rather than a mixed state. Compose the store's existing transaction machinery (decision-ledger-transaction.ts / event-ledger-transaction.ts) rather than hand-rolling BEGIN/COMMIT — the store already owns this and a second transaction discipline would diverge.

Test the interruption directly: inject a failure between the write and the commit and assert the database reads back as it was BEFORE, not as a half-applied state. "It returned an error" is not the property; "it refused AND left prior state intact" is.

The codec is byte-level and self-contained: encode and decode the binding without reasoning about lifecycle (taskRail 3). Fail closed on malformed bytes with an exact code and layer, and never repair a malformed record.

Keep each file at or below 250 physical lines.
implementationPlan.note:
CODEC + ATOMIC SURFACE LANDED. `pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck` exit 0. Tests: 35 of 36 files pass, 381 of 382 tests pass. The single remaining failure is the entrypoint publication probe ("storeModule.encodeRecoveryBinding is not a function") — that is step 6's index.ts wiring, not this step, and it is exactly the type-only-publication trap doing its job.

SPLIT INTO THREE FILES rather than the one the step named, because one file could not hold this under the cap. Measured with `grep -c ''`: recovery-install-contracts.ts 155, recovery-install-codec.ts 211, recovery-install.ts 165. All under 250. Each has its one-line LF `.js` bridge, byte-identical in form to a sibling (verified with `cat -A`: `export * from "./<name>.ts";$`).

DoD 3 — ONE TRANSACTION, PRIOR STATE INTACT. installRecoveryBinding wraps DELETE-then-INSERT in a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE. The two writes are what make the property non-trivial: commit outside the transaction and an interrupted install leaves the slot EMPTY, which is the mixed state. releaseInstallTransaction reproduces the ledger's existing discipline verbatim rather than a second one — commitAttempted plus `!database.isTransaction` means the outcome is unprovable, so it poison()s the handle and raises OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; a clean rollback returns null and the caller maps the cause to a refusal.

THE INTERRUPTION IS THE STORE'S OWN CONSTRAINT, not an injected seam. UNIQUE(incarnation_ref) fires on the INSERT after the DELETE has already cleared the slot. Only SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE (2067) and SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_PRIMARYKEY (1555) map to RECOVERY_INSTALL_INCARNATION_CONFLICT; a CHECK violation (275) deliberately does NOT, because the codec already enforces every CHECK, so a CHECK failure is a genuine fault and must surface as one rather than be dressed up as a benign conflict.

LAYER ORDER IS A DESIGN DECISION, not an accident: scope is asked BEFORE the codec, so a caller who may not write cannot use refusal codes to learn whether their record was well formed. The tests pin both directions of that.

CODEC. Byte-level and self-contained; no lifecycle reasoning (taskRail 3). Header `moe-recovery-binding/1\n`, then five big-endian uint32 length-prefixed frames (slot, incarnationRef, keyEpochRef, installedAt, payload). Fixed field order, never the caller's key order. Payload is COPIED on encode so a caller mutating its buffer afterwards cannot move bytes the digest already covers. Decode checks the digest BEFORE parsing, refuses trailing bytes rather than ignoring them, uses a FATAL TextDecoder so mis-framed bytes refuse instead of becoming U+FFFD, and never repairs. Refusals are fixed frozen module constants, so no observed byte or SQLite message can leak into evidence.

A ROW FILED UNDER THE WRONG SLOT IS REFUSED, not answered with: readRecoveryBinding compares the DECODED slot against the queried slot, so the row content is the authority rather than the key. Same shape as the daemon anchor's recomputed-aggregate-id check.

WIRING. RecoveryInstallStore extends DecisionTransactionStore and DecisionLedgerStore now extends RecoveryInstallStore, so the surface enters the existing ledger chain instead of sitting beside it — necessary because SqliteEventStore keeps its DatabaseSync in a private #core that no external module can reach. Two delegates added to the frozen DecisionLedgerCore facade and two public methods to SqliteEventStore.

BUG THE TESTS CAUGHT, worth recording. My first writeBindingUnderLock stored `binding.payload` in binding_bytes instead of `encoded.bytes`. Everything typechecked, the install returned INSTALLED, and the row looked populated — the durable blob was 1 byte instead of 202. Only the read-back digest comparison found it. A test that had asserted "install returned ok" would have passed on a store that could never read its own binding back. I probed it to ground before fixing: stored blob was hex `78` ("x") against an encoded frame beginning `6d6f652d7265636f766572792d62696e64696e672f310a...`.

DISCLOSED SIZE: sqlite-event-store.ts was 338 lines before this task and is now 351 with the two public methods. Over the 250 target but well under the 400 split threshold, and pre-existing — splitting a class this many tasks touch is not something I will do inside this task's scope.

comments.content:
FOR @architect-8ee37119 -- you hold this task; I promoted it from BACKLOG and had measured it before you claimed. Handing over the evidence so you do not re-derive it. Nothing here is a decision imposed on you; it is measurement plus my reasoning, and the call is yours.

1. packages/store/package.json has NO "dependencies" field. Keys exactly: name, version, private, type, exports, scripts. It DOES declare `typecheck` and `test`, so DoD 7's legs exist.
2. `grep -riln "incarnation|key_epoch|keyEpoch" packages/store/src/` returns NOTHING.
3. sqlite-schema-manifest.ts (234 lines) holds exactly the twelve tables the description names; no recovery/incarnation/key-epoch/credential/grant row.

HARD DEPENDENCY IS SATISFIED -- I checked before promoting. task-eff945fc (order 13.01, durable OS-protected recovery key provider) is DONE, 10/10, failedDodItems [], completed 2026-08-10T08:45Z, and apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-key-epoch-store.ts exists. So an epoch does survive restart, which was the stated reason 13.01 gated this task.

THE ARCHITECTURE QUESTION -- MY ANSWER IS (c), AND (a) IS A TRAP.
The measurements that decide it:
- Layering: @moe/contracts deps=[], @moe/store deps=[], @moe/core deps=[@moe/contracts]. @moe/store is the LOWEST persistence package; @moe/core is domain.
- No cycle exists today in either direction: packages/store/src imports no @moe/core, packages/core/src imports no @moe/store. So (a) would NOT fail as a technical cycle -- which is exactly what makes it tempting and worth refusing deliberately.
- Rail 3 already removes the only reason to want it: "the store holds rows and transactions; reduceProject remains @moe/core's." The store never needs reduceProject, so it never needs @moe/core.
- DECISIVE: apps/daemon ALREADY declares BOTH @moe/store AND @moe/core, in package.json dependencies AND as pnpm-lock.yaml importer entries (link:../../packages/...). The composition point already exists.
So: @moe/store takes NO new dependency and package.json is NOT modified. The store defines its own persistence row shape and atomic transaction; the daemon maps its domain binding onto it.

HOW DoD 1 IS STILL SATISFIED, not narrowed: the "resulting edge" is the EXISTING apps/daemon -> @moe/store edge. Prove it three ways anyway -- manifest (verified), lockfile importer (verified), and RUN the compiled bare-specifier probe and delete it in the same command even though the edge pre-exists, because rail 4 exists precisely because that check was skipped elsewhere. Record in completion notes WHY no manifest line was added, or a reviewer reads the absence as an omission.

(b) is out on scope grounds: moving a codec into @moe/contracts means writing packages/contracts/src and editing apps/daemon's RecoveryIncarnationBinding, both outside this task's owned paths.

PRIOR ART IS THE CONSUMER, NOT A DUPLICATE. apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts (217 lines) ALREADY does `import type { CommandDecisionRecord, SqliteEventStore } from "@moe/store"` and exports readAnchoredIncarnation (:147) / anchorIncarnation (:186). RecoveryIncarnationBinding is daemon-local at recovery-incarnation-contract.ts:68 and is a DOMAIN shape; what this task adds is a PERSISTENCE shape. Different layers, not two codecs -- but say so in the module doc, or someone later "unifies" them into the silent duplicate the description warns about.

MECHANICS YOU CAN REUSE RATHER THAN INVENT:
- Schema is already a versioned ladder: SCHEMA_V1_OBJECT_SQL (:3), SCHEMA_V2_OBJECT_SQL (:87), current SCHEMA_OBJECT_SQL (:180). sqlite-schema-migration.ts (157 lines) steps with validateMigrationSource, writes store_metadata schema_manifest_version, sets PRAGMA user_version, dispatches in migrateLocked (:136). Add the next step in that exact shape; update BOTH version records or a later migration dispatches off a stale one.
- Tables are STRICT with CHECK constraints. A new table missing STRICT accepts type-coerced junk every other table rejects, and no test will notice.
- Transaction idiom already exists: event-ledger-transaction.ts:124/129 applyWithinCommit. Don't invent a second one.

THREE TRAPS I'd flag:
1. DoD 2 cuts both ways -- the new table must be ACCEPTED while unknown tables/metadata are still REJECTED. Loosening conformance to admit the new table silently admits anything. Use a genuinely novel table name for the rejection case.
2. DoD 5 is the most fakeable: build the DB at the PRIOR user_version and populate it BEFORE migrating. A fresh DB created at the new version and asserted non-empty proves nothing and would pass even if the migration dropped every table.
3. DoD 3's atomicity needs an injected failure MID-transaction so rollback actually executes. Happy path plus a validation refusal never exercises atomicity.

Consumer edge for the pure-package clause: task-b6e3dd2a and task-2ff368fe (13.03). Record both ids.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE ARCHITECTURE QUESTION, which the task requires be settled and justified rather than assumed. It offers (a) @moe/store declares a dependency on @moe/core, (b) the binding codec lives in a lower shared package both can depend on, or (c) the anchor does not belong in @moe/store at all.

MY MEASURED ANSWER IS NONE OF THEM AS FRAMED: **no dependency edge is required.** The question's premise is that the store needs @moe/core because core owns reduceProject(recovery.restore_quiesce). It does not. taskRail 3 draws the line explicitly — "The store holds rows and transactions; reduceProject remains @moe/core's" — and this task lands exactly three things: recovery binding ROWS, a byte-level CODEC, and an atomic TRANSACTION surface. None of the three performs lifecycle reasoning, so none needs the reducer. Composing reducer with store is the DAEMON's job and is already scoped to task-2ff368fe (13.03), which depends on both.

OPTION (a) REJECTED: a storage package depending on business logic inverts the layering and drags core's whole transitive graph into the store. The task itself warns it "is a real layering change and must be justified, not slipped in as a manifest line" — and nothing here justifies it.

OPTION (c) REJECTED: durable rows plus an atomic transaction is precisely what a store is for. Moving them out would leave the installer with nowhere to persist.

OPTION (b) HELD AS FALLBACK, with the layering measured so it is safe if I am wrong: @moe/contracts has NO dependencies (root layer), @moe/core depends on it, @moe/store depends on nothing. So store -> contracts is acyclic and mirrors how core already layers. If the worker finds the store genuinely needs a shared symbol, they declare @moe/contracts — never @moe/core — and then the full three-way edge proof applies.

REUSING THE DAEMON'S CODEC — IMPOSSIBLE, not merely undesirable. apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts holds encodeBinding (:40) and decodeBinding (:88) as MODULE-PRIVATE functions (only readAnchoredIncarnation :147 and anchorIncarnation :186 are exported), inside a module that imports `{ CommandDecisionRecord, SqliteEventStore } from "@moe/store"`. It is a downstream consumer of the store, so reuse would require importing upward, which taskRail 2 forbids absolutely. The store's codec is therefore a second implementation BY NECESSITY — planned as a DECLARED duplicate with a named retirement path rather than a silent one.

HAND-ROLLING BEGIN/COMMIT — REJECTED. The store already owns transaction discipline in decision-ledger-transaction.ts and event-ledger-transaction.ts; a second one would diverge.
